title: A signal about sodium
hook: Connect a hormonal signal with a target.

knows: Hormones can carry signals through the blood to target tissues.
doesNotKnow: Aldosterone acts on parts of the kidney to promote sodium reabsorption and influences potassium secretion.

misconception: All hormones come from one gland and act on every cell.
objective: Identify the stated endocrine signal and its target in a simplified pathway.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: Which adrenal-cortex hormone promotes sodium reabsorption in the kidney? Aldosterone acts on parts of the kidney to promote sodium reabsorption and influences potassium secretion.
The diagram shows one selected source–target pathway, not all hormone effects or feedback loops.
Recall: In the stated example, which source releases Aldosterone into the circulation? Aldosterone acts on parts of the kidney to promote sodium reabsorption and influences potassium secretion.

recall.question: In the stated example, which source releases Aldosterone into the circulation?
recall.why: Aldosterone acts on parts of the kidney to promote sodium reabsorption and influences potassium secretion.
